lens: Short-form vertical micro-drills (TikTok-style): 30-second objection reps in a feed
name: Cockpit and Drill Feed
one_liner: A dark, instrument-panel live call with 30-second objection drills as the daily habit, backed by a schema-first persona library that contributors extend through pull requests and Codex.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed: the 30-second objection rep is the unit of practice. It becomes a vertical snap feed that serves as the front door, the daily habit and the shareable clip. Changed: a feed cannot carry the coaching depth of a 5 to 15 minute call, so the live cockpit stays the core and the feed sits on top as a funnel and retention layer. Competitor pages (Second Nature, Yoodli) set live-deal coaching and enterprise controls as the bar, which pushed the core toward a control-room aesthetic rather than a pure feed.

design_language.typography: Geist for UI and display: 600 for headings, 500 for body. Body 15/22, page H1 28/34, landing display 40/44. Geist Mono for timers, scores, timestamps and transcript times. Replaces Sora and Inter.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 14px card radius, 10px for controls, pill chips. 1px line borders. Resting cards have no drop shadow; depth comes from stepping from surface-900 to surface-800. Teal glow is reserved for the live element.
design_language.motion: Springs (stiffness 300, damping 30) for score roll-ups. Coach cues slide in from the right in 240ms. The drill timer ring fills linearly over 30 seconds. Under prefers-reduced-motion, the rubric flash becomes a colour change and springs become fades.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 20px in controls, 1.75 stroke. No emoji in the UI. Each job family gets a simple monoline glyph, so the library scans without stock photos.
design_language.theme_modes: Dark is the default, with a full light theme. Both use CSS variables on :root with overrides for [data-theme=light] and prefers-color-scheme. A print stylesheet forces light for the debrief, so the existing Print button stays useful.

navigation_and_ia: Desktop: a 64px icon rail that expands to 232px, with Drills, Library, Practice, Progress and Team (org admins only). The top bar holds Cmd+K and a model ribbon. live_coaching_and_scoring: Architecture: the persona voice is forbidden to coach. Voice runs on OpenAI Realtime, added as a provider beside the existing ElevenLabs Agents path. A sidecar coach reads the rolling transcript each turn and returns zod-validated JSON: cue, objection tag, rubric deltas and next question. Cues must quote a transcript line, are rate-limited to one per 20 seconds, and are suppressed while the rep is speaking. Live scores are labelled live est. and replaced by the evidence-backed grade afterwards, so the two never silently disagree. If the coach fails, the cockpit shows Coach offline and the call continues. Self-score D: 5.5. This meets the baseline on design. It exceeds only if p95 cue latency is under about 2 seconds and the quote check passes on sampled calls.
persona_library_and_wizard: Schema first: each persona is one YAML file (persona, scenario, talk track, objections, rubric, voice), validated by zod and published as JSON Schema under /personas, so contributors add one by pull request. Launch seed: about 150 personas across 16 job families (SDR cold call, AE discovery, SaaS, insurance, mortgage, real estate, solar, home services, auto, medical devices, B2B procurement, recruiting, retail, customer success, collections, custom), three difficulty levels, and a 30-second drill variant for each. Filters: job, industry, difficulty, objection, mode, length. The wizard uses structured outputs to return that schema, marks every generated field and cites its source. Self-score E: 5.4, conditional on at least 100 reviewed personas shipping. Below about 60, it falls short.
signature_moments: Thirty-second drill: a ring fills while you answer, and the score plus one quoted line lands in under five seconds.
The +4 flash on a live rubric bar when you ask a discovery question, which teaches the rubric by feel.
Click any evidence quote in the debrief and the replay timeline jumps to that exact second.
Remix on any persona forks it into a PR-ready YAML draft, so the library itself is the contribution door.
A Copy Codex prompt button on each persona card gives a ready-to-run prompt for tuning that persona locally.
openai_fund_angle: Make OpenAI the default stack and show it. The landing page and cockpit ribbon name the models in use (voice, grading, coach, wizard), with per-call tokens and a cost estimate, which shows reviewers and users what the credits buy. Attribute with text ('Built on OpenAI models') and do not use the OpenAI logo unless its brand guidelines permit it. Put Codex in the repo, not just the UI: an AGENTS.md, Codex review on persona and rubric pull requests, Codex-drafted release notes, and Codex Security scans of the auth and MFA code. The Codex for Open Source program page lists PR review, maintainer automation and release workflows, so link real PRs from a /docs/codex page. Invite contributors with a good-first-persona label, the YAML template and the Copy Codex prompt button. Caveat: the program terms say benefits are granted at OpenAI's sole discretion. The aggregator lists up to $25K in API credits, while the OpenAI program excerpts I saw name a $1 million fund and no per-project cap. Verify before submitting.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 0 (about 1 week): move tokens into tailwind.config.ts, load Geist, add shadcn primitives behind the existing routes, retire Sora and the .card and .btn-primary classes. Phase 1: cockpit and coach sidecar behind a flag, with the mobile cockpit in parallel. Phase 2: YAML persona schema, 100 to 150 reviewed personas, library and wizard. Phase 3: drill feed, debrief replay, progress and manager views. Keep existing route paths so deep links survive.

risks: Business self-scores: F1 SaaS 5 (crowded by Second Nature, Hyperbound and Yoodli; viable only as open-core with a hosted team tier). F2 selling to entities 6 (budgets exist, but buyers expect SSO/SCIM, SCORM/LTI and SOC 2 per vendor pages; a persona-pack licence is the cheapest first deal). F3 not worth building 3 (worth building if scope stays on the cockpit and library).
Scope: nine screens, a feed, a wizard and two voice providers is too much for one release. Ship the cockpit and the library first and let the feed follow.
Coach latency and cost: a sidecar call per turn can lag or overspend. Measure p95 and cap cues per minute.
Content quality: generic personas will hurt credibility. A review gate and a contributor rubric are required before the 100-persona threshold counts.
Gimmick risk: a TikTok-style feed can read as a toy to enterprise buyers. Keep it a drill module, not the whole app.
Research gap: Mobbin returned no live-coaching-during-call screen. The cockpit is extrapolated from Delphi, Descript and SchoolAI patterns, not a proven reference.
Competitor claims here come from vendor-authored comparison pages (Second Nature, Yoodli, Mindtickle) and are unverified.
Dark-first can hurt print and classroom projection. The light theme and print stylesheet are required, not optional.
